name: Kpanlogo
notes: Kpanlogo style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). A rare and beautiful thing: a traditional African drum-dance with a NAMED CREATOR — kpanlogo was created in the early 1960s by OTOO LINCOLN, a young Ga man in Bukom, Accra, who built it with friends from Ga rhythms, highlife energy, and rock-and-roll swagger for a newly independent Ghana's youth. The elders called it indecent; in 1965 the dancers famously performed it for review and Ghana's Arts Council (under Nkrumah's government) approved it — the youth dance won its place, and today kpanlogo is danced at Ga festivals, schools, and university African ensembles worldwide. This pack keeps the creator credited (traditional does not mean anonymous — the same lesson as Afrobeats' named moves, one generation earlier), teaches the openly-taught recreational form: the low-swinging basic, the bell pattern that everything locks to, the invitation gestures, and the drum-break stops. The kpanlogo bell rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping the kpanlogo bell pattern through one track, then stepping the basic against it.
Film the kpanlogo basic — bent knees, swinging arms, one full song without rising out of it.
Film the invitation gestures and travels over the basic — playful, storytelling, unhurried.
Film a drum-break run: dance, hit the stop, hold the picture, resume — five times in one track.
Find kpanlogo live: a Ghanaian cultural group, a university African drum-and-dance ensemble, a Ga festival. Tell someone who made it.

attributes.name: Low-swing knees L1
attributes.test: 90s of dancing with knees bent and level — kpanlogo lives low; rising out of it is the tell of a tired dancer

attributes.name: Bell-lock ear L1
attributes.test: clap the kpanlogo bell pattern along to a track for two minutes without drifting — the bell is the truth everything locks to

nodes.name: The bell pattern — the truth-keeper
checkpoints: kpanlogo locks to a bell timeline — the pattern every drum and every dancer measures against; it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
West African ensemble logic: the bell never solos and never stops, and that's why it's in charge
clap the bell until it's boring, then step against it — boredom in the hands is readiness in the feet

nodes.name: The kpanlogo drums & the break
checkpoints: the kpanlogo drums (peg-tuned, congas' Ga cousins) layer parts over the bell; the lead drum calls the BREAKS — sharp phrases that stop and restart the dance
learn the break by ear: the call is unmistakable once you've heard three — everyone hits the stop together and grins
highlife and Ga street energy share this groove: your practice playlist spans 60 years of Accra

nodes.name: Ga Accra — the ground it grew from
checkpoints: kpanlogo is a GA dance — the Ga people of coastal Accra, whose fishing neighborhoods like Bukom raised it and whose older drum-dance traditions (kolomashie and gome among them) fed it
it lives in the Ga recreational repertoire: festivals, community celebrations, and the Homowo season's joy — a social dance, openly shared, distinct from the Ga rites that are not
when ensembles abroad teach kpanlogo, the good ones say 'Ga, from Accra' in the first sentence — so does this app

nodes.name: Otoo Lincoln — the man who made it
checkpoints: kpanlogo was CREATED in the early 1960s by OTOO LINCOLN, a young Ga man in Bukom, Accra — built with friends from Ga rhythms, highlife, and rock-and-roll swagger for independent Ghana's youth
traditional does not mean anonymous: one generation before Afrobeats' named moves, a named young person made a 'traditional' dance — credit him the way this app credits every creator
the name itself traces to a story-song Lincoln told — the dance came with its own folklore built in

nodes.name: 1965 — the youth dance wins its place
checkpoints: elders called the new dance indecent — the hip swings scandalized, as every youth dance from waltz to twist has scandalized
in 1965 the dancers performed kpanlogo for review and Ghana's Arts Council under Nkrumah's government approved it — the young people argued with their bodies and won
today it's danced at Ga festivals and taught in schools and university ensembles worldwide: yesterday's scandal is today's heritage, which is most of how heritage gets made

nodes.name: The kpanlogo basic — the low swing
nodes.anchor: the step the whole dance lives in
checkpoints: knees bent, body pitched easy forward, feet stepping the pulse while the arms swing low and loose in opposition — the whole dance breathes from this
stay LOW and level: the head doesn't bob; the knees absorb everything
the hips swing free — that's the part that scandalized 1964, and it's not optional
lock the step to the bell, not the drums — the drums decorate; the bell decides
mistakes: standing tall (kpanlogo danced upright is kpanlogo not yet danced)
stiff arms (the swing is the style — let them be heavy and easy)

nodes.name: Invitation gestures & play
checkpoints: over the basic, kpanlogo speaks in playful gestures — beckoning hands, pointing, mimed story moments traded across the circle
gestures are invitations: you throw one at someone and the circle watches them answer — solo practice means throwing them at the mirror and answering yourself
keep the feet honest while the hands talk — the basic never pauses for the story

nodes.name: Travels & level changes
checkpoints: the basic travels: circling steps, forward surges, and dips lower still — the low swing goes places without rising
level discipline: travel happens through the knees, the head staying on one smooth rail
orbit a spot like the circle is real; enter and exit the imagined center like it's someone's solo turn

nodes.name: Hitting the breaks
checkpoints: when the lead drum calls the break, the dance STOPS — a held picture, a beat of grinning stillness, then everyone resumes together
train it: dance the basic, have a friend (or a random timer) call stops, and freeze clean without wobble
the resume matters as much as the stop: back into the bell's pocket on the first beat, not the third
mistakes: coasting through the break (the stop is the dance's punctuation — miss it and the sentence runs on)

nodes.name: The Bukom set — filmed
checkpoints: film one full track: low-swing basic locked to the bell, gestures telling something, one travel circuit, and every break hit clean
level check on review: does your head ride one rail, or does it bob when you tire?
say 'kpanlogo, made by Otoo Lincoln, Bukom, Accra' on camera — the credit is part of the set

nodes.name: The live circle
checkpoints: find kpanlogo live: Ghanaian cultural associations, university African drum-and-dance ensembles, and Ga festival celebrations teach and dance it openly
a live drum circle is the real classroom — the bell in the air beats the bell in your headphones
teach one person the basic and tell them who made it — heritage moves by exactly this mechanism
